title: A scalar tagged through a %TAG handle keeps its tag and its directive when its value is replaced
notes: The tag `!e!foo` resolves through the `%TAG` directive to `tag:example.com,2000:foo`. The new value `yes` is a string and still a scalar, so reading it back under that tag gives exactly the value that was set and the tag stays (a kit convention, docs/edit-semantics.md: a custom tag on a scalar stays while the new value is a scalar). The directive is outside the node and is not touched. `yes` is a string in the core schema, so it is written plain.

provenance.reference: Differential testing of the oneyaml-python native and pure backends; the native backend dropped the tag and wrote `yes`; the pure backend wrote the expected bytes.
